findings.description: Typo in canonical text name: 'Analerta 12.11' should read 'Analects 12.11' (Confucian Analects, Lunyu)
findings.suggestion: Replace 'Analerta' with 'Analects' — the text referenced carries the title Analects of Confucius (论语)
findings.context: Confucian *ren* (benevolence) and *li* (ritual propriety) require that authority flow through relationships of mutual obligation, not unilateral command (Analerta 12.11).

findings.description: Strong unqualified claim: 'autonomous AI systems reproduce every element of this dynamic' asserts complete mapping without evidence of exhaustive comparison
findings.suggestion: Hedge to match the evidence: 'autonomous AI systems reproduce key elements of this dynamic' or 'autonomous AI systems exhibit structurally parallel dynamics' — the post demonstrates strong parallels but 'every element' claims completeness the analysis does not verify
findings.context: Ninety-four years later, autonomous AI systems reproduce every element of this dynamic.

findings.description: The SNAFU Principle gets cited from Shea & Wilson (1975) without noting that the source text — The Illuminatus! Trilogy — functions as satirical fiction. Readers unfamiliar with the source may treat this as formal organizational theory rather than literary provenance that later entered organizational discourse
findings.suggestion: Add a brief genre note: 'what Robert Shea and Robert Anton Wilson (1975) named the SNAFU Principle in their satirical novel *The Illuminatus! Trilogy* — a concept that subsequently entered organizational theory discourse' — this preserves attribution while surfacing the literary origin
findings.context: Robert Shea and Robert Anton Wilson (1975) called the SNAFU Principle: in any hierarchical organization, information flowing upward gets distorted in proportion to the power differential between sender and receiver.

findings.description: The phrase 'This framing ignored several inconvenient facts' presents inference as observation. The framing may have deliberately excluded these facts, or proponents may have been unaware of them, or they may have considered and weighed them differently — 'ignored' presumes intent
findings.suggestion: Replace with factual description: 'This framing omitted several countervailing facts' or 'This framing did not account for several relevant facts' — both describe the gap without attributing intent
findings.context: This framing ignored several inconvenient facts. The ICESCR does not prescribe any particular economic system.

findings.description: ICESCR abbreviation appears in the body text (line 68) without expansion. The summary expands it, but readers entering the body directly encounter an unexpanded abbreviation. Each post should stand independently for readers who arrive via direct link
findings.suggestion: On first body use, expand: 'The International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights (ICESCR) addresses structural violence directly...'
findings.context: The ICESCR addresses structural violence directly by establishing obligations around work, education, healthcare, and an adequate standard of living.

findings.description: UDHR abbreviation appears in body text (line 58) without expansion. Same issue as f5 — readers arriving directly encounter an unexpanded abbreviation
findings.suggestion: On first body use, expand: 'The Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) drafting committee likely included people...'
findings.context: The UDHR drafting committee likely included people who had encountered this correspondence

findings.description: The term 'holdouts' carries negative evaluative framing — it presumes non-ratification represents a failure rather than a policy position. In a descriptive historical context, a neutral term would strengthen fair witness compliance
findings.suggestion: Replace with neutral language: 'The United States occupies a small and shrinking cohort of non-ratifying states' or simply 'nations that have not ratified'
findings.context: The United States occupies a small and shrinking cohort of non-ratifiers. The other notable holdouts include a handful of small island states and countries in active conflict.

findings.description: The claim 'the U.S. effectively declared that freedom of speech counts as a fundamental right but the right to food, housing, and healthcare does not' infers a declaration from an omission. The U.S. may have declined ratification for procedural, political, or institutional reasons (as the companion post documents) rather than making an affirmative judgment about rights hierarchy
findings.suggestion: Strengthen the hedge: 'the U.S. in practice prioritized civil and political rights over economic rights' or 'the practical effect created a hierarchy that the UDHR drafters explicitly rejected'
findings.context: By separating economic rights from civil rights and ratifying only one, the U.S. effectively declared that freedom of speech counts as a fundamental right but the right to food, housing, and healthcare does not.

epistemic_flags: Vocabulary findings (f5, f6) assume readers arrive at individual posts via direct link; series readers who follow the navigation order encounter expansions in the companion post
Register finding (f7) applies fair witness standards to an advocacy site — the evaluative framing may represent a deliberate editorial choice rather than an oversight
